questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Recombinant DNA Technology Foundations' refers to.
questions.a: Genetic engineering collects every method that edits nucleic acid directly, and it became practical once Stanley Cohen's plasmid delivery into E. coli met Herbert Boyer's restriction-enzyme cutting that leaves matching single-stranded termini - together, in 1973, they closed a foreign gene into a cut plasmid and created the first recombinant molecule, aided by ligase discovered in 1967.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Recombinant DNA Technology Foundations'.
questions.a: Cut with restriction enzymes, join with ligase, and carry the construct in a plasmid - the cut-paste-clone logic behind all rDNA work.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Recombinant DNA Technology Foundations' taught, and from which source text?

Work with: completion_year = 200, earlier_year = 100, later_year = 100, start_year = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of tech_gap.
Explain in your own words what 'Milestones Timeline of Modern Biotechnology' refers to.
questions.a: The subject advanced in dated leaps: Ereky coined the name in 1917, Avery's team fixed DNA as genetic material in 1944, Lederberg found plasmids in 1952, Watson and Crick solved the helix in 1953, Berg assembled the first recombinant DNA in 1972, Mullis invented PCR in 1983, Humulin won approval in 1982, the human genome project ran from 1990 to 2003, and the CRISPR-Cas9 Nobel arrived in 2019-2020 after the mRNA vaccine work.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Milestones Timeline of Modern Biotechnology'.
questions.a: Subtract one milestone year from another to measure how fast the field moved between landmarks.

Explain in your own words what 'Therapeutic Proteins from rDNA Technology' refers to.
questions.a: Recombinant production replaced gland harvesting: where tons of pancreas once yielded only milligrams of insulin and thousands of pituitaries a little growth hormone, bacteria now brew human insulin (approved as Humulin in 1982) and growth hormone free of animal contaminants; interferon fights cancer while plasminogen activator and urokinase dissolve dangerous blood clots.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Therapeutic Proteins from rDNA Technology'.
questions.a: Human genes in microbial hosts give safer, cheaper and limitless supplies of proteins once rationed from animal glands.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Therapeutic Proteins from rDNA Technology' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: E. coli Division versus Genome Replication Timing

questions.q: Using the method 'E. coli Division versus Genome Replication Timing', work with: elapsed_min = 240, generation_time = 300, replication_time = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of generations.

Take the relation taught for 'E. coli Division versus Genome Replication Timing' and work with: elapsed_min = 10, generation_time = 200, replication_time = 45. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of generations.
Explain in your own words what 'E. coli Division versus Genome Replication Timing' refers to.
questions.a: Escherichia coli finishes a division every twenty minutes yet needs about sixty minutes to copy its chromosome, an apparent paradox the cell resolves by running several replication forks in parallel (multifork replication), so each daughter still inherits a complete copy on schedule.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'E. coli Division versus Genome Replication Timing'.
questions.a: Divide replication time by generation time to see how many forks must run at once.

concepts.title: Genetically Modified Crops and Plant Products

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Genetically Modified Crops and Plant Products' refers to.
questions.a: Targeted edits in plant genomes gave farmers crops that shrug off disease, drought and salinity - the Flavr Savr tomato of 1994 opened the era, Monsanto's Bt cotton reached fields in 1996 and India by 2003, and Golden Rice carrying provitamin A appeared in 2000 - while rDNA technology now promises therapeutic proteins grown in plants at low cost and free of animal pathogens.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Genetically Modified Crops and Plant Products'.
questions.a: One inserted gene can buy resistance, nutrition or shelf life - and plants may become the cheapest bioreactors of all.
